title: U.S. House · California's 9th Congressional District
area: Part of the Central Valley centered on Stanislaus and San Joaquin counties, including Modesto, Turlock, and Manteca.

context.text: This district's boundaries changed under California Proposition 50, the mid-decade congressional redistricting measure voters approved in November 2025. Incumbent Josh Harder and Republican John McBride advanced from the June 2, 2026 top-two primary, defeating Martin Veprauskas, Khalid Jeffrey Jafri, and Parminder Singh.

candidates.name: Josh Harder
candidates.ballotNote: Won the June 2, 2026 top-two primary with about 61% of the vote.
candidates.currentRole: U.S. Representative for California's 9th Congressional District (since 2023; previously the 10th District, 2019-2023)

summary.text: Josh Harder is the Democratic incumbent representing California's 9th Congressional District, a Central Valley seat based around Modesto and Manteca. He serves on the House Committee on Appropriations and is running for re-election focused on lowering costs, health care, and water issues in the Valley.

background.text: Born in Turlock, California; graduated from Modesto Public High School.
Earned a bachelor's degree in political science from Stanford University in 2008 and master's degrees in business administration and public policy from Harvard University in 2014.
Worked as a course instructor at Modesto Junior College, vice president of Bessemer Venture Partners, and a consultant with The Boston Consulting Group before being elected to Congress in 2018.

priorities.text: Says he is focused on lowering costs, delivering affordable health care, bringing home good-paying jobs, addressing homelessness, and keeping neighborhoods safe.

Says he is fighting to stop the Delta Tunnel water project, which he describes as a "water grab" that would ship Valley water to Los Angeles, and to build new water storage while protecting the Delta.
priorities.quote: The Delta is the lifeblood for the valley and everything we do. It's our economy's livelihood.

priorities.text: Says he authored the Ban Corporate PACs Act and is working on campaign-finance reform.

positions.summary: Campaign site says he supports a $35-per-month cap on insulin costs and measures to bring down prescription drug and health care costs.

Says climate change is an existential threat and that he introduced the FARM Act, which he describes as backed by both environmental and agricultural groups, to help Valley farmers address climate change.

Says he supports a pathway to citizenship for Dreamers and comprehensive immigration reform, while also calling for strong border security and enhanced technology to stop drug smuggling and trafficking.
Says he stands with law enforcement and helped secure federal funding for a task force targeting methamphetamine and fentanyl trafficking and for new police officers and equipment.

record.text: Assigned to the House Committee on Appropriations, Subcommittee on Labor, Health and Human Services, Education and Related Agencies, and Subcommittee on Interior, Environment and Related Agencies, in the 119th Congress (2025-2026).
Sponsored the Ban Corporate PACs Act, which would prohibit corporate political action committees from contributing to federal candidates.

candidates.name: John McBride
candidates.ballotNote: Won the June 2, 2026 top-two primary with about 23% of the vote.

summary.text: John McBride is a strength and conditioning coach and the Republican nominee for California's 9th Congressional District, campaigning on reducing government spending, border security, and support for law enforcement.

background.text: Born in Meriden, Connecticut; earned a bachelor's degree from Central Connecticut State University in 1984.
Career experience includes working as a strength and conditioning coach.

priorities.text: Campaign site lists reducing what he calls oppressive tax policies, shrinking government spending, and supporting small business under "Economy."
Lists "Safer Communities" as a priority, including support for local law enforcement, a stronger southern border, and mental health initiatives.
Lists agricultural water rights and reducing government influence on small, private farms under "Agriculture."

positions.summary: Campaign site lists a "stronger southern border" and support for criminal prosecution under his public-safety priorities.
Campaign site calls for reducing what he describes as oppressive tax policies and no tax on Social Security, alongside drastically shrinking government spending.
Campaign site lists support for local law enforcement among his "Safer Communities" priorities.
